original_idea: Um diário reflexivo que ajuda a capturar sensações sutis do dia a dia, medindo se o tempo de resposta do editor de texto abaixo de 16ms reduz a distração ao digitar.
current_idea: Um diário reflexivo que registra sensações sutis do cotidiano e avalia, por meio de um índice de distração baseado em desempenho de digitação e prompts reflexivos semanais, se fatores como velocidade e taxa de erro reduzem a distração ao digitar.
human_intent: Criar um diário reflexivo que registre sensações sutis e avalie se um tempo de resposta do editor abaixo de 16 ms reduz a distração ao digitar.
problem_statement: Distração ao digitar devido à latência do editor de texto, dificultando a captura de sensações sutis do dia a dia.
assumptions: Latência abaixo de 16 ms pode ser percebida pelos usuários
Usuários conseguem identificar e registrar sensações sutis
É possível medir a distração de forma objetiva
ambiguities: Como definir e quantificar “distração” ao digitar
Qual método será usado para medir o tempo de resposta do editor
Qual plataforma ou dispositivo será utilizado
strengths: Uso de métrica objetiva de latência
Atenção às experiências subjetivas do usuário
Possibilidade de validar empiricamente o impacto da latência

critical_issues.issue: Latency below 16 ms is unlikely to be perceptible by most users, making the core metric ineffective.
critical_issues.why_it_matters: If users cannot notice the latency difference, the measured correlation with distraction becomes meaningless, undermining the diary's purpose.

critical_issues.issue: No validated method exists to objectively measure distraction while typing.
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Without a reliable metric, any claimed reduction in distraction cannot be substantiated, rendering the evaluation invalid.

critical_issues.issue: Assuming users can consistently identify and record subtle daily sensations is unrealistic.
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Inconsistent or inaccurate entries will corrupt the dataset, leading to false conclusions about latency effects.

critical_issues.issue: Hardware and OS variability will cause latency measurements to fluctuate beyond the 16 ms threshold.
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Uncontrolled variance introduces noise, making it impossible to isolate latency as a causal factor for distraction.

fragile_assumptions: Latency below 16 ms can be perceived by users
Users can reliably identify and log subtle sensations
contradictions: The system claims to measure distraction objectively while relying on subjective self‑reports of sensation
It assumes latency is a primary cause of distraction despite no evidence that other factors (e.g., UI design) dominate
failure_modes: Latency sensor reports inaccurate values due to OS scheduling delays
Users abandon the diary because the required introspection feels burdensome
Data analysis misattributes reduced distraction to latency when other variables changed
Privacy breaches expose sensitive personal reflections

alternatives.mechanism: Calibrated relative latency and keystroke‑dynamics monitoring
addresses_issues: Latency below 16 ms is unlikely to be perceptible by most users, making the core metric ineffective.
No validated method exists to objectively measure distraction while typing.
Hardware and OS variability will cause latency measurements to fluctuate beyond the 16 ms threshold.
tradeoffs: Adds computational overhead for real‑time keystroke analysis
Potential privacy concerns with detailed typing behavior
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Moves from an absolute 16 ms threshold to device‑specific relative latency changes and behavioral proxies

alternatives.mechanism: Controlled micro‑delay experiment with immediate self‑report
addresses_issues: Latency below 16 ms is unlikely to be perceptible by most users, making the core metric ineffective.

tradeoffs: Self‑report may be biased by demand characteristics
Limited ecological validity due to artificial delays
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Introduces intentional latency manipulations to directly test perceptibility rather than relying on passive measurement

alternatives.mechanism: Wearable physiological sensing combined with diary entries
addresses_issues: No validated method exists to objectively measure distraction while typing.
Assuming users can consistently identify and record subtle daily sensations is unrealistic.

tradeoffs: Requires users to wear additional hardware
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Adds multimodal physiological markers (HRV, skin conductance) to infer distraction, reducing dependence on self‑report and software latency

alternatives.mechanism: Performance‑based distraction index using typing speed/error rates and weekly reflective prompts
addresses_issues: Latency below 16 ms is unlikely to be perceptible by most users, making the core metric ineffective.
No validated method exists to objectively measure distraction while typing.
Assuming users can consistently identify and record subtle daily sensations is unrealistic.
Hardware and OS variability will cause latency measurements to fluctuate beyond the 16 ms threshold.
tradeoffs: Requires longer data collection periods to detect patterns
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Replaces latency measurement with aggregate performance metrics and higher‑level weekly reflections, simplifying data collection while still targeting distraction reduction
